newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FORECAST-Chubais sees jump in Russian unemployment.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Chubais sees jump in Russian unemployment.

text.p: Unemployment in Russia may rise significantly in 1998 if the government succeeds in implementing economic reforms, Interfax news agency quoted First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais as saying on Thursday.
"Starting from 1998 we are in for a serious worsening in unemployment rates," Interfax quoted Chubais as telling a cabinet meeting.
According to the State Statistics Committee currently there are only 2.53 million officially unemployed people in Russia.
But many people do not register as unemployed and many of those who are registered as employed work short weeks.
The government estimates total unployment at 6.99 million or 9.7 percent of the workworce, according to the methodology used by the International Labour Organisation.
However, the government always expected the unemployment rates to be low.
"We have been seriously mistaken in the last three years in our forecasts of unemployment, which turned out to be higher than expected," Chubais said.
He asked the State Employment Fund to get ready for higher unemployment rates.
